```bash
mkdir Archived_Quarter1
```

> **Result**: A new empty folder named `Archived_Quarter1` appears in your current directory.

---

### 2️⃣ Find all `.txt` files in `Quarter1_Reports`

```bash
find Quarter1_Reports -name "*.txt"
```

> **Output** (example):
> ```
> Quarter1_Reports/report1.txt
> Quarter1_Reports/report2.txt
> Quarter1_Reports/summary.txt
> ```

> These are the full paths of the text files you want to copy.

---

### 3️⃣ Copy each file into `Archived_Quarter1`

For each file listed above, run:

```bash
cp Quarter1_Reports/report1.txt Archived_Quarter1/
cp Quarter1_Reports/report2.txt Archived_Quarter1/
cp Quarter1_Reports/summary.txt Archived_Quarter1/
```

> **Result**: Each file is now duplicated inside `Archived_Quarter1`.  
> The original files remain untouched in `Quarter1_Reports`.

---

### 4️⃣ Verify the copy

```bash
ls Archived_Quarter1

> ```
> report1.txt
> report2.txt
> summary.txt
> ```

| Step | Command | Purpose |
|------|---------|---------|
| 1 | `mkdir Archived_Quarter1` | Create destination folder |
| 2 | `find Quarter1_Reports -name "*.txt"` | List all text files |
| 3 | `cp <source> Archived_Quarter1/` | Copy each file |
